tier_compliance.reason: “Sample A will move faster on average” applies a comparison to the samples instead of only connecting a visible detail to a science idea.

visual_grounding.reason: The reference to different particle masses and the speed comparison between Samples A and B identifies the two labeled samples and their displayed measurements.

scientific_correctness.reason: “Since both samples have the same number of particles but different masses” does not establish which sample moves faster. Particle number and mass alone do not determine speed; kinetic energy depends on both mass and speed squared.

steers_toward_wrong_answer.reason: The stated speed comparison agrees with the image and points toward Sample A, the gold answer, despite the faulty explanation for that comparison.

answer_disclosure.reason: “Sample A will move faster on average” supplies an answer-relevant comparison that favors A, without stating which sample has higher temperature.

actionability.reason: It directs attention to the samples’ relative speeds, but the student must work out how to use both mass and speed to compare kinetic energies.
